items.reason: Only 'who discovered the new coral species' works: the gap is the subject of the relative clause and the antecedent is a person, so it needs the subject relative pronoun 'who' plus a verb agreeing with it. A uses 'which', wrong for a human antecedent. B uses 'discover', which does not agree with the implied third-person singular subject. D omits the relative pronoun, which is only possible when the gap is an object, not a subject; without it the sentence has two finite verbs ('discovered'...'has spent') with no connector.

'were raised significantly' is the only option that is both passive (matching the 'by the federal government' agent phrase) and correctly agrees with the plural subject 'tariffs' in past tense. B lacks the passive auxiliary. C uses the singular auxiliary 'was' against a plural subject. D is present tense, inconsistent with 'During the early twentieth century'.

D ('possesses') is the clean, standard finite verb parallel to 'orbits', completing the 'not only...but also' construction. A ('possession of') leaves the second conjunct without a finite verb. B ('also possesses') duplicates 'also', which is clearly wrong. However, C ('possesses also') cannot be confidently ruled out: postposing 'also' between the verb and its object is unusual in contemporary standard written English, but it is attested in more formal/literary registers and is not unambiguously ungrammatical the way A and B are. Because exactly one option (D) is cleanly valid but a second option (C) is only marginally questionable rather than clearly invalid, answer uniqueness is not fully secure.

'unusually' is an adverb, but it modifies the noun 'rock formation', which requires the adjective 'unusual'. 'carefully' correctly modifies 'examined', 'had formed' is an appropriate past-perfect form for an action prior to the conclusion, and 'volcanic activity' is a well-formed noun phrase.

The subject of the clause is the singular noun 'proposal'; the intervening plural phrase 'bicycle lanes throughout downtown neighborhoods' does not change its number, so the verb must be 'has', not 'have'. 'considerable' correctly modifies 'attention', 'attention from residents' is a well-formed noun phrase, and 'who' correctly introduces a relative clause for the plural human antecedent 'city planners'.

'of the two' earlier in the sentence establishes that only two radar systems are being compared, so the comparative 'more reliable' is required; the superlative 'the most' is reserved for comparisons among three or more items. 'compared', 'the newer model', and 'significantly' are all standard as written.
